items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: I got Benny Morton on trombone... we played a lot of theatres... Lena got good money for all of the theatres that we played

ctx.x: Now you say that he was using a number of your arrangements that you had had with your own band, and then he augmented that band. Did you do -- continue arranging while you were working with him or was --

Yes. He let me write anything I wanted to, and of course, my book was quite instrumental in keeping the job because we had to build a new library. Only thing that happened -- I had to make the extra parts for the extra men when he augmented the band. In fact, one of the guys is quite active now that was in that group -- Benny Morton, the trombone player.

items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: I made quite a few records with him. And, of course, Benny Morton Billy Martin was on that great eight piece band that backed Lena Horn when I was playing with Lena Horne

ctx.x: And he owned (inaudible) quite a bit of it -- anyhow, I got this DownBeat, and I saw where he and -- Benny Morton been replaced by somebody else, man, in this group (inaudible). had so what he's doing now, I don't know, but he sounds like Benny because Benny never liked the road, if I remember correctly. He was -- when I first met Benny, he was one of the four guys that -- when Don Redman took my band over, and we went to Connie's Inn. He was one of the four additions that Don added to the because he had 3…

So he could always play, and I made quite a few Benny. records with him. And, of course, Benny Morton Billy Martin was on that great eight piece band that backed Lena Horn when I was playing with Lena Horne (inaudible), you know, and at the Capital Theater with this band that I think we discussed about a few days ago that, there were eight pieces. And those That was a tremendous size. And salaries Lena had me assembled together these four and Benny was in that boys, group.

items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: He's just Benny Morton Martin, you know. He likes home. And I don't think that he's changed.

ctx.x: But when you're talking about months and months, and no way, and he was a typical New Yorker. He loved New York. He was brought up on the East Side, you know, and he talks that language, you know. He's just Benny Morton Martin, you know. He likes home. And I don't think that he's changed. I'd be willing to bet on that. He's one of the few that didn't care about the one nighters, one of those things, and he's always been in demand around New York. -- recording with the different bands and all that.
